original_card.question: Can one precisely specified helper-mixing word satisfy a replacement for the inherited H2/K interface?
methods: Derive a replacement interface lemma and price its implementation.
Seek an exact dirty-input or chronological-cut counterexample to the proposed replacement.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A full boundary contract and paid profile; unchanged scalar counts alone are insufficient. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Compare the two false H2/K flags with the unchanged paid profile in its README.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write one replacement H2/K implication for a single helper-star operation, then try to falsify it on dirty inputs.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A legitimate replacement could admit a cheaper bit circuit; scalar savings alone do not alter the selected moment.
allowed_variations: Choose one helper-star or quartet instance; narrow to one boundary implication.
scope_change_triggers: Changing only source count or scalar addition count without an interface argument.

actual_scope: Sharp integer pricing, at the +10% bit endpoint c* = 921658892752012102303/5e23 of centre-sharing-overhead-budget, of each catalogued revision-3 bit lever changed one premise at a time on the actual PR589 histogram (surcharge recomputed): halving-depth cap raise, width-8 re-hosting in the actual idle windows, copy carriage/count, two-call bit centre sharing with its overhead budget, unpaid coordinates, helper deletion (two local models, optimal re-hosting) and ideal local shapes; plus the complex-side two-call overhead budget at the same endpoint. Second method: levers.py interval arithmetic on independently rebuilt histograms.
scope_change_reason: The card's H2/K helper-interface question is saturated by other packages; this answers the explicit, unowned open question 1 of centre-sharing-overhead-budget (PR1791), which decides whether the strongest complex lever (two-call centre sharing) can be part of a +10% route. That needs a bit lever netting at least 649 rank-1 units on the actual histogram, which no package had priced.
bottleneck_link: Two-call centre sharing makes the bit side bind; +10% kappa needs the bit endpoint 0.0018433. No admitted bit lever nets anything there (halving-depth cap slack at max window 42, record hosting optimal, rank-8 carriage loses 2,578 units); clearing 649 needs a new word/decoder: one fewer rank-7 copy per call, bit-side two-call centre sharing (overhead <= ~29.1 units/call), >= 40 pure helper deletions per call, >= 649 doubly-unpaid families, or ideal shapes in >= 52 of 288 calls. The complex half of the route must keep its sharing overhead <= ~28.3 units/call at that endpoint. No kappa claim.
stop_rule: Stop once the lever table is exact and the primary (D/E-diagnostic engine) and independent (levers.py) methods agree on every pass/fail sign at c* and c* + 1e-24; build no construction and search for no new bit word.
evidence: RESULT.json: requirement 649 rank-1 (648 fails) / 16 rank-42; (a) caps 45/50/53, max child 42 = max window, net 0; (a') per-slot costs 7.94284 < 7.94625 < 7.95184 rank-1 units, record optimal, net 0; (b1) cst 72: -2577.6; (b2) 93 copies sharp (92 fails), one fewer per call +2008.8; (b3) cst 31.5: +9039.5, overhead budget 8391 rank-1 / 1203 rank-7 / 201 rank-42; (c) F >= 649 families; (d) RANK1 40 per call (39 fails for every hosting), TEMPLATE exhausted by d = 19 at +169.8; (e) 52 of 288 calls (51 fails), all calls +3647.6; complex k=2 overhead at c*: 4079 rank-1 / 511 rank-8 (28.3-28.4 units per call). 40 signs reproduced by independent.py.
